summary:
Sweden's parliament approved new acts on legal gender recognition and on medical procedures performed on genitalia in April 2024, the Library of Congress global legal monitor records; the Riksdag vote on the gender-recognition law was 234 in favour to 94 against.

The Legal Gender Recognition Act came into force on 1 July 2025. It lowers the minimum age for changing legal gender without a gender-dysphoria diagnosis from 18 to 16, requires a statement from a doctor or psychologist together with approval from the National Board of Health and Welfare, and requires guardian approval for applicants aged 16 and 17. TGEU's assessment of 16 July 2025 is that the act simplifies the procedure but falls short of a full self-determination model, with medical barriers remaining, so a visitor seeking to update legal documents may still have to satisfy medical conditions.

The same package of legislation limits genital surgery to adults aged 18 and over and removal of the gonads to those aged 23 and over, absent exceptional reason.

Sweden's main national board decided on 28 January 2017 that transgender people would no longer be classified as mentally ill. That depathologisation step governs diagnostic status for trans residents and for visitors whose home jurisdiction still requires a diagnosis.

Transgender identity and expression were added to Swedish hate crime legislation on 1 July 2018, and to the hate speech provisions effective 1 January 2019; sexual orientation had been added to the hate crime provisions in 2010 and to the hate speech law by a Riksdag vote in 2002, effective 1 January 2003. Enforcement of the sexual-orientation provisions has been criticised as selective: authorities declined to prosecute a Halmstad imam who called homosexuality a virus in 2015, and a Pentecostal preacher convicted over a sermon was ultimately acquitted when the Supreme Court held that religious-speech protections under the European Convention barred punishment.

The clearest documented everyday-facility friction concerns changing rooms. SVT reported in October 2025 that the swimming-pool chain Medley stopped trans customers from choosing their changing rooms, an access restriction trans visitors should expect at that chain's facilities.

Restrictions on gender-affirming care for minors are administrative rather than statutory. The Karolinska Institute stopped providing puberty blockers or gender-affirming hormone therapy to children and teenagers under 16 in March 2021, and to 16 to 18-year-olds outside approved clinical trials. On 22 February 2022 the National Board of Health and Welfare said puberty blockers should be used only in exceptional cases backed by uncertain science; this is guidance, not a ban. In 2021 the Board reduced the number of gender-affirming clinics from seven to three. Misinformation that Sweden had banned gender-affirming care for minors has circulated on social media and been cited by politicians in the United States to justify outright bans, and the claim is not supported by the sources.

Sweden also records a documented rise in domestic anti-gender campaigning. The Sweden Democrats and the Christian Democrats oppose trans-rights legal reforms while framing that opposition as protecting women's rights and Swedish values, and gender-critical radical feminist groups are organised through the Swedish Women's Lobby, an umbrella for 57 associations representing over 130,000 women and girls, which in 2025 launched the Women's Platform for Action International promoting sex-based rights. Scholars document what they call an insidious de-democratisation and report growing political violence and intimidation against trans advocates, feminist scholars and racialised activists, including online harassment, threats and public vilification.
tangentialFactors:
Third-party standing remains high: the 2019 edition of the Spartacus Gay Travel Index, reported by Newsweek, ranked Canada, Portugal and Sweden as the most LGBT-friendly travel destinations.

Brå, the National Council for Crime Prevention, published report 2024:13 in January 2025, a descriptive analysis of persons suspected of offences in which police identified LGBTQI-related hate-crime motives. The dataset covers LGBTQI motives as a whole rather than trans victims separately.

ILGA-Europe's Annual Review 2026, covering 2025, records that a bill would extend protection of victims of conversion practices where those are carried out through coercion, threats or sustained psychological pressure, and that in November the Church of Sweden decided new priests must be willing to marry same-sex couples, passing 141 votes at the 2025 Church Council.

Military service conditions rest on a long policy history: an open-access article in Sexuality Research and Social Policy of 4 February 2016 traces LGBT policy development in the Swedish military from 1944 to 2014.

The wider legal background includes legalisation of same-sex sexual activity in 1944, with the age of consent equal at 15 since 1972, and declassification of homosexuality as an illness in October 1979. Until 2013 a legal gender change required sterilisation and sex reassignment surgery; those requirements were ruled unconstitutional in January 2013 and removed by the Riksdag in July 2013, and roughly 600 to 700 people were later compensated 225,000 SEK each under a law passed in March 2018 for forced sterilisation.

Anti-gender actors also target knowledge production, labelling gender studies and intersectional feminist scholarship ideological or unscientific, and the movement's framing travels internationally: misinformation about Swedish policy on minors has been used abroad to argue for bans.
localsOnly:
Depathologisation of transgender status took effect through the national board's decision of 28 January 2017, so residents are not classified as mentally ill on that basis. One open-coverage source dates the declassification inconsistently, to 2017 in one passage and 2009 in another.

Residents seeking a legal gender change must obtain a doctor's or psychologist's statement and National Board of Health and Welfare approval, with guardian approval for those aged 16 and 17; TGEU's position is that medical barriers remain despite the simplified procedure.

State-facing support exists for LGBTQ residents: a 1978 state inquiry into the living conditions of gays and lesbians proposed granting refugee status to persecuted LGBTQ people, and RFSL counselling centres in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö assist people with contact to authorities and legal assistance with matters such as asylum and wills.

A 2021 study found that migrant LGBTQ people in Sweden report worse sexual health, avoid healthcare more often, are more exposed to sexual violence and are more dissatisfied with their sexual life than other groups.

Nationwide National Board of Health and Welfare data released in 2026 showed that trans children prescribed puberty blockers had increased slightly since the 2022 guidance.

Domestic advocacy carries a documented cost. Scholars and sources record online harassment, threats and public vilification aimed at trans advocates, feminist scholars and racialised activists, alongside organised gender-critical mobilisation through the Swedish Women's Lobby and its 2025 international platform.
outOfScopeNotes:
No visa, entry or border-screening rules for LGBTQ travellers appear anywhere in the source inventory; whether admission or residence decisions turn on gender identity or trans status is not sourced here and remains unresolved.

The sources do not state how often the hate crime and hate speech provisions covering transgender identity and expression have been applied, and the only documented enforcement failures concern sexual orientation rather than trans victims.

The coverage of declassification of transgender status as an illness is internally inconsistent, giving both 2017 and 2009; the 2017 date is the one carried by the contemporaneous news report.

It is not sourced whether the Medley changing-room restriction reported in October 2025 is chain-wide policy, site-specific, or has since been changed, and no regulator or court response to it is recorded.

The status and fate of the conversion-practices bill noted for 2025 is unresolved in the inventory; the sources describe the bill but not its passage.

Whether the reduced set of three gender-affirming clinics has been designated, and what wait times a visitor or resident would face, is not covered.
